---
title: "Prelude"
subtitle: "What to do before 9 September"
---

Everything on this page is designed to be done **on your own laptop, before
the workshop**. Budget about two hours in total, spread over a few evenings.

::: {.callout-important}
## The one thing that must be done
Install R, RStudio and Quarto, and run the setup check. If your laptop is not
ready on the morning of Day 1, you will spend the first session watching
downloads instead of writing code.
:::

## Checklist

| | Task | Time | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| ☐ | Install R, RStudio, Quarto | 30 min | [Install the software](install.qmd) |
| ☐ | Install workshop packages and run the check script | 15 min | [Check your setup](check-setup.qmd) |
| ☐ | Work through the self-paced R primer | 45 min | [R primer](r-primer.qmd) |
| ☐ | *Or*, work through the interactive primers instead — they run in your browser, so a laptop whose R install has not succeeded yet is no obstacle | 45 min | [Interactive primers](primer-01-objects.qmd) |
| ☐ | Download the workshop datasets | 5 min | [Datasets](data.qmd) |
| ☐ | Skim the pre-reading | 20 min | [Pre-reading](pre-reading.qmd) |
| ☐ | Complete the online pre-test | 10 min | *link circulated by the SET Team* |

::: {.callout-tip title="Do the interactive primers before you travel"}
Working through all five pages downloads about 35 MB in total (Primer 5, with
its plotting engine, accounts for most of that). Your browser caches it for a
week, so opening them at home makes them instant at the venue — conference
wifi shared by forty people is not the moment to find out. They need **no
installation at all**, which makes them a good place to start if your laptop
setup has not gone smoothly yet — you can keep learning while you sort it out.
:::

## What to bring

- A laptop you have **administrator rights on** (you will be installing
  software). Windows, macOS and Linux are all fine.
- A charger. Power outlets are limited; arrive charged.
- At least **5 GB free disk space**.
- Your institutional email, for the R and Quarto ecosystems that ask for one.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Institutional laptops
If your IT department locks down installation, contact the SET Team **at
least one week before** the workshop. A cloud fallback
([Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud), free tier) can be arranged, but a local
installation is strongly preferred — that is what you will use afterwards.
:::

## What you do *not* need

- Prior programming experience of any kind.
- Statistics beyond what you already use in your own research.
- A paid licence for anything. Every tool in this workshop is free and
  open source.

## Why a prelude at all

Two days is short. Installation problems, "what is a working directory?", and
"why does my file not open?" can eat half of Day 1 — and they are exactly the
problems that are easiest to solve alone, in advance, without an audience.
Doing the prelude buys us the time to spend Day 1 on ideas instead of
plumbing.

::: {.callout-note}
## Stuck?
Work through [Troubleshooting](../resources/troubleshooting.qmd) first — it
covers the errors that account for most installation failures. If that does
not help, email the SET Team with (a) your operating system and version,
(b) the exact error message, and (c) the output of `sessionInfo()`.
:::
